Scholarly Name Reference

कर्ण Karṇa

also written Karna

A king of Aṅga and the elder half-brother of the Pāṇḍu princes on the mother's side — the son of the sun-god Sūrya by Kuntī (Pṛthā) before her marriage with Pāṇḍu.

The Authentic Name of Karṇa

Scholarly reference for Karṇa

Devanagari

कर्ण

The name in its original Devanagari form. कर्ण → Karṇa. Sanskrit Karṇa is written in Devanagari as कर्ण · IAST transliteration maps each Devanagari vowel and consonant to a Latin equivalent · Macrons mark long vowels (ā, ī, ū); dots beneath consonants mark retroflex articulation (ṭ, ḍ, ṇ, ṣ)

ASCII Constraint

KARNA

Stripped of its identity, the name was reduced to plain Latin letters. The original orthography — stress, length, breathing — was erased by systems that only understand A-Z.

Unicode Restoration

Karṇa

The Unicode restoration recovers what ASCII destroyed. This is philological accuracy — not decoration. The domain encodes to Punycode, but the browser displays the truth.

Name Senses
Etymology Ear, earrings

The name carries more than one valid sense. The primary sense is the figure or role; the etymology is the older linguistic root.

Punycode Encoding
karṇa.com → xn--kara-de5a.com

The non-ASCII characters in Karṇa are encoded while the ASCII remains visible. To the DNS, it is Punycode. To humanity, it is Karṇa. PUNICODEX does not claim this domain is available; always verify status with a registrar.

Saying It
KAHR-nah · /ˈkar. ɳa/

Derived from restored orthography (classical Sanskrit / IAST).

Tier Classification

Why Karṇa is classified as Tier-1

The Sanskrit restoration कर्ण preserves at least one distinctive feature its ASCII form loses — a diacritic or a distinctive letter that marks the original phonology. This makes it a single-tier Tier-1 name.
